{
  "extractions": [
    {
      "unit": "F001:F004",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001"],
        "scope_text": "Applies to an employee of a covered employer seeking status as an eligible employee.",
        "context_quotes": ["F003", "F004"],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F002", "F003", "F004"],
        "choice_quote": "F002:F004",
        "choice_text": "All three criteria must be met: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months, AND (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, AND (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.",
        "logic_quote": "F002:F004",
        "references": ["§ 825.801", "§ 825.105(b)"],
        "statement": "An eligible employee is defined as an employee of a covered employer who meets three cumulative conditions: has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F005",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F001", "F002", "F005"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for the required 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": ["F006"],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the applicable break-in-service rules are met."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F006",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005", "F006"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of 29 CFR 825.110.",
        "context_quotes": ["F007:F009"],
        "modality_quote": "need not",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F006",
        "references": ["paragraph (b)(2)"],
        "statement": "Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of 29 CFR 825.110, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F007:F009",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005", "F007"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where a break in service is more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": ["F006"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": ["F008", "F009"],
        "choice_quote": "F008:F009",
        "choice_text": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted where either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation, OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.",
        "logic_quote": "F008:F009",
        "references": ["USERRA, 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."],
        "statement": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or where a written agreement exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F008",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F007", "F008"],
        "scope_text": "Where an employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F008",
        "references": ["USERRA, 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."],
        "statement": "The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, though this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F005"],
        "scope_text": "When calculating the weeks of employment toward the 12-month employment requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F010",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment, and 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months for determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": [],
        "scope_text": "When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "Nothing in this section prevents",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Employers are permitted to consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F011"],
        "scope_text": "If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment preceding a continuous break in service of more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F012"],
        "scope_text": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of 29 CFR 825.110 and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": ["paragraph (c)(2)", "§ 825.801", "29 CFR part 785"],
        "statement": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the FLSA for determining compensable hours of work, based on the number of hours worked within the meaning of the FLSA rather than limited by recordkeeping methods or inaccurate compensation agreements."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": ["F012"],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the requisite 1,250 hours of service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F013"],
        "scope_text": "In determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave for an employee returning from USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": ["F013"],
        "modality_quote": "shall",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": ["§ 825.801(c)"],
        "statement": "An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, adding those hours to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F013"],
        "scope_text": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "can generally",
        "modality": "possible",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": ["§ 825.801(c)"],
        "statement": "To determine the hours that would have been worked during a period of absence due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F014"],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F014",
        "references": ["29 CFR part 541", "§ 825.102", "§ 825.801(d)"],
        "statement": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F015"],
        "scope_text": "When evaluating whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and the 12-month employment requirement.",
        "context_quotes": ["F015"],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": ["§ 825.300(b)"],
        "statement": "The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": ["F015"],
        "scope_text": "When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "would",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": ["§ 825.300(b)"],
        "statement": "An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave."
      }
    }
  ]
}

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee of a covered employer seeking status as an eligible employee.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All three criteria must be met: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months, AND (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, AND (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is defined as an employee of a covered employer who meets three cumulative conditions: has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for the required 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the applicable break-in-service rules are met.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of 29 CFR 825.110.
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of 29 CFR 825.110, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where a break in service is more than seven years.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted where either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation, OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation, or where a written agreement exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Where an employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer, though this section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When calculating the weeks of employment toward the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer, the week counts as a week of employment, and 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months for determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Employers are permitted to consider employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: If an employer chooses to recognize prior employment preceding a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of 29 CFR 825.110 and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the FLSA for determining compensable hours of work, based on the number of hours worked within the meaning of the FLSA rather than limited by recordkeeping methods or inaccurate compensation agreements.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service under FLSA principles.
unit_attributes.statement: Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the requisite 1,250 hours of service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave for an employee returning from USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, adding those hours to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: To determine the hours that would have been worked during a period of absence due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements.
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When evaluating whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave.
